
- Type: Object Storage.
- What it solves: The need for unlimited, accessible storage. Unlike a hard drive, S3 doesn't have a file system (no C:/ drive). It uses "**Buckets**" (containers) and "**Objects**" (files). It is designed to store terabytes or petabytes of data that you can access via a URL.
- The "Form" details:
- Storage Classes: Solves for cost vs. access speed.

|Storage Class|Access Latency|Durability (AZs)|Min Duration|Cost Tier|Best Use Case|
|S3 Standard|Milliseconds|3+ AZs|None|High|Frequent access: Active app data, static website assets, big data.|
|S3 Express One Zone|Single-digit ms|1 AZ|None|Highest|Ultra-high performance: ML training, financial modeling, real-time analytics.|
|S3 Intelligent-Tiering|Milliseconds|3+ AZs|None|Variable|Unpredictable patterns: Data with changing or unknown access frequencies.|
|S3 Standard-IA|Milliseconds|3+ AZs|30 Days|Moderate|Infrequent access: Long-lived backups, disaster recovery files.|
|S3 One Zone-IA|Milliseconds|1 AZ|30 Days|Low|Non-critical data: Secondary backups or data that can be easily recreated.|
|S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval|Milliseconds|3+ AZs|90 Days|Very Low|Rarely accessed archive: Medical images or news media needing instant access.|
|S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval|Minutes to Hours|3+ AZs|90 Days|Extremely Low|Standard archive: Regulatory data requiring retrieval within minutes to hours.|
|S3 Glacier Deep Archive|12 to 48 Hours|3+ AZs|180 Days|Lowest|Deep archive: Long-term (7–10 year) retention for compliance.|

- Lifecycle Policies: Solves for automation. You can set a rule: "After 30 days, move this file to cheaper storage."

# Access Management & Security

## Default Encryption vs. Bucket Policies
SSE-S3 encryption is automatically applied to new objects stored in S3 Bucket.
- Optionally, “force encryption” using a bucket policy an refuse any API call to Put an S3 object without encryption headers (SSE-KMS or SSE-C)
- Bucket policies are evaluated before “Default Encryption.”
## Access Controls
- User-Based (IAM Policies): Apply to specific users or groups to control which S3 API actions they can perform
- Resource-Based (Bucket Policies): Bucket-wide JSON policies configured directly on the S3 Bucket
	- Required for cross-account access or enforcing strict security conditions
- Access Control Lists (ACLs): A legacy, fine-grained access tool that AWS recommends disabling in favor of bucket policies
- [[AWS Organizations]] (Service Control Policies (SCPs)): Sets maximum allowable permissions (guardrails) across accounts. Multi-account and Organizational Units.




![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Amazon S3 Encryption

- Sever-Side Encryption (SSE)
	- Server-Side Encryption with Amazon S3-Managed Keys (SSE-S3) - Enabled by Default
	- Encrypts S3 objects using keys handled, managed, and owned by AWS
	- Object is encrypted server-side
	- Encryption type AES-256
	- Default for new buckets & new objects
- Server-Side Encryption with [[AWS Key Management Service (KMS)]] Keys stored in AWS KMS (SSE-KMS)
	- Leverage AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage encryption keys
	- KMS advantages: user control + audit key usage using CloudTrail
	- Must set header “x-amz-server-side-encryption”: “aws:kms”
	- Limitations
	- When uploading calls GenerateDataKey KMS API
	- When downloaded, it calls the  Decrypt KMS API
	- Count towards KMS quota per second Quotas Console
	- Can request a quota increase using the Service
- Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C)
	- When you want to manage your own encryption keys
	- Amazon S3 does NOT store the encryption key you provide
	- HTTPS must be used
	- Encryption key must provide HTTP headers, for every HTTP request made
	- Can only be done through the CLI
- Client-Side Encryption
	- Clients must encrypt data before sending to Amazon S3
	- Clients must decrypt data themselves when retrieving from Amazon S3
	- Encryption in transit (SSL/TLS)
	- Encryption in flight is also called SSL/TLS
## Encryption in Transit (SSL/TLS)
- Amazon S3 exposes two endpoints:
	- HTTP Endpoint - non encrypted
	- HTTPS Endpoint - encryption in flight
		- HTTPS is recommended
		- SSE-C HTTPS is mandatory
		- Can force encryption in Transit
To prevent man in the middle (MITM) attacks and comply with the [Domain 1 Secure Architecture]. Protect buckts by attaching a bucket policy containing a Deny statement that blocks requests where the global condition "aws: SecureTransport" evaluates to "false"

## Multi-Factor Authentication MFA Delete

- Force users to generate a code on a device (usually a mobile phone or hardware) before doing important operations on S3
	- MFA is required to
		- Permanently delete an object version
		- Suspend Versioning on the bucket
	- MFA not required to
- Enable Versioning
- List deleted versions
- MFA Delete, Versioning must be enabled on the bucket
- Only the bucket owner (root account) can enable/disable MFA Delete

# The Solution: Amazon S3 Tiers

## S3 Durability, Availability, Replication Mechanics (CRR & SRR)

- High durability = the average expectation to incur loss of an object.
- Availability = How readily available and accessible a service is.

## Replication Mechanics (CRR & SRR)
Many organizations replicate buckets to different destinations for disaster recovery and compliance.
- Replication Rules:
	- Must enable Versioning on both the source and target buckets
	- Replication is asynchronous and can copy objects across different AWS accounts
	- Enabling replication only copies new objects.
		- To copy objects prior to enabling, you must deploy S3 Batch Replication
	- Cross-Region Replication (CRR): 
		- Used to satisfy geographical compliance guidelines
		- minimize access latency for gloval users
	- Same-Region Replication (SRR):
		- Highly utilized for log aggregation
		- Production-to-test synchronizations
		- Syncing data across different account ownership boundaries in the same region
	- How deletions work: 
		- Delete an object without version ID creates a delete marker
			- Can configure S3 to replicate these delete markers.
			- deleting a specific object version ID is not replicated to prevent accidental  or malicious data loss
	- No Chaining: Replication is strictly direct
		- E.G. Bucket A replicates to Bucket B then Bucket B to Bucket C in a linear fashion
# S3 Access Logs vs [[AWS CloudTrail]]

### S3 Access Logs
- For audit purposes
- Logs all requests, accounts, authorized, or denied
- Data can be analyzed using tools
- Target bucket must be in the same Region
# S3 Sub-Features
- **S3 Versioning**: When enabled, the bucket maintains different variants of an object within the same bucket. This acts as a safeguard against overwrites and deletions.
	- Bucket-Level Setting
		- Once enabled, the setting is permanent
		- can be suspended
	- Requirement for Cross-Region Replication (CRR)
	- Composite Lookup Key + Bucket + Key + Version ID.
	- S3 Deletion Mechanic
		- When Versioning is enabled, an object is NOT permanently deleted.
			- A deleted marker is placed on the object
			- The Delete Market is now the Current Version of the object
			- Performing standard "Get" command will yield "404 Not Found"
			- Restore by deleting Delete Marker; the previous version will become the current version'; the version without the Delete Marker.
		- MFA Delete
			- Requires physical/Virtual MFA key to permanently delete a version ID or suspend bucket versioning
			- Can only be configured using the AWS Account Root User via CLI/API
	- Lifecycle Policies for Nonconcurrent Version: Every version of an object is still it's own object.
		- Each copy/version of an object incurs storage cost
		- Adjusting Lifecycle rules can help minimize cost 
			- move noncurrent versions to lower tiers to lower cost.
- **S3 Batch Replication**: only applies to objects that have been stored after the replication rule has been created. Batch replication allows for asynchronous replications of existing objects, objects that have previously failed to replicate or objects already replicated to be relocated to a targeted destination.
	- Powered by S3 Batch Operations.
	- The Manifest File
		- A list that tells S3 what to copy.
	- Replication Status Overrides
		- Unlike standard live replication, Batch replication can re-replicate objects despite status
			- statuses:
				- completed
				- Failed
				- Replica
			- Can target certain statuses
				-E.G replicate only failed objects

- **S3 Transfer Acceleration: Bucket-level feature designed to speed up long-distance uploads/downloads between a client and S3 Bucket
	- Utilizes [[Amazon Cloudfront (Content Delivery Network (CDN))]] to route to the nearest [[Edge Location]]
	- [[Private AWS Backbone]]: utilizes internal, highly optimized, low-latency route via AWS Global Fiber Backbone
	- Can be used as a high speed [[VPC Endpoints]]
- Multi-Part Uploads
- S3 Analytics
- S3 Storage Lens
- S3 Lifecycle Policies
- **S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR): replicates data across [[AWS Availability Zones (AZ)]] within the same [[AWS Region]] 
	- Doesn't protect from regional failure
	- Improves avaialability
- **S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR): automatically replicates every object uploaded to a bucket in one [[AWS Region]] to a bucket in a different [[AWS Region]]

# Storage Service Comparison
|Storage Service|Architecture Level|Concurency Limits|Regional Scope|Best Use Cases|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Amazon EBS**|Block Storage|Connected to **one** EC2 instance at a time (except raw Multi-Attach io1/io2)|Locked to a **single AZ**|OS boot volumes, databases (RDS/self-managed), transactional low-latency workloads|
|**Amazon EFS**|Network File Storage|Shared concurrently by **hundreds/thousands** of EC2 instances|**Multi-AZ** by default|Web servers (WordPress), shared code repositories, home directories, media processing|
|**Amazon S3**|Object Storage|Access is serverless via **HTTPS APIs** from anywhere on the web|**Global namespace**, replicates across 3+ AZs|Static website hosting, raw data lakes, backup archives, media delivery backing|
